tip: Улыбающаяся (ulybayushchayasya = smiling) is a participle used like an adjective, agreeing with женщина (zhenshchina = woman) in gender and case.
Открытое (otkrytoe = opened) is a past passive participle used like an adjective, agreeing with окно (okno = window).
A passive participle names its agent in the instrumental: приготовленная мамой (prigotovlennaya mamoy = prepared by mom).
Не зная (ne znaya = not knowing) is an adverbial participle; it marks action going on at the same time as the main verb.
The -в ending on Позавтракав (pozavtrakav = having had breakfast) marks an action completed before the main verb пошли (poshli = went).
This verb takes о plus prepositional: мечтая о путешествиях (mechtaya o puteshestviyakh = dreaming about travels).
A predicate noun after быть (byt = to be) takes the instrumental: будучи врачом (buduchi vrachom = being a doctor).
Reflexive verbs form the adverbial participle in -вшись: проснувшись (prosnuvshis = having woken up), from проснуться (prosnutsya = to wake up).
Russian always puts a comma before что (chto = that) in reported speech: сказали, что согласны (skazali, chto soglasny = said that we agree).
A request uses чтобы plus a past-tense verb: чтобы мы подождали (chtoby my podozhdali = for us to wait), not an imperative.
Indirect questions keep the original tense: приедем (priedem = will arrive) stays future, where English uses 'would arrive'.
For a yes/no indirect question, put ли (li = whether) after the key word: можно ли войти (mozhno li voyti = whether one may enter).
Russian keeps the spoken tense: уезжает (uezzhaet = is leaving) stays present, where English shifts to 'was leaving'.
The -ся verb Считается (schitaetsya = it is considered) is an impersonal passive: no subject, action stated generally.
Past passive uses был plus a short participle: был перенесён (byl perenesyon = was postponed).
In a passive, the agent takes the instrumental: посажены школьниками (posazheny shkolnikami = planted by schoolchildren).
Age uses the dative: сколько вам лет (skolko vam let = how old are you), literally 'how many years to you'.
по plus dative means 'according to': по его словам (po ego slovam = according to him).
который (kotoryy = who) takes gender from брат (brat = brother) but its case from its own clause; as subject here it stays nominative.
Material uses из plus genitive: построен из кирпича (postroen iz kirpicha = built out of brick).
